question: To what baseline models is proposed model compared?

evidence: TF-IDF: We applied TF-IDF features as inputs to four classifiers: support vector machine classifier (SVM), logistic regression classifier (LR), Naive Bayes classifier (NB) and random forest (RF); CNN: We followed the same architecture as BIBREF9; LSTM: We applied an LSTM model BIBREF20 to classify the sentences with pre-trained word embeddings;LSTM-soft: We then added a soft-attention BIBREF21 layer on top of the LSTM model where we computed soft alignment scores over each of the hidden states; LSTM-self: We applied a self-attention layer BIBREF22 to LSTM model. We denote the content vector as $c_i$ for each sentence $i$, as the input to the last classification layer.

We conducted a comprehensive comparison with the baseline models, and some of them were never investigated for the abbreviation disambiguation task. We applied traditional features by simply taking the TF-IDF features as the inputs into the classic classifiers. Deep features are also considered: a Doc2vec model BIBREF19 was pre-trained using Gensim and these word embeddings were applied to initialize deep models and fine-tuned.

title: A Neural Topic-Attention Model for Medical Term Abbreviation Disambiguation
answer_short: Naïve Bayesian classifier (NB), LSTM with self attention model (LSTM-self)
answer_rationale: Text 3 (page=6, section=Evaluation) explicitly states that the second group of experiments used neural models, where LSTM with self attention model (LSTM-self) was chosen as the base model. Text 3 also mentions that the first group of experiments used TF-IDF features for traditional models, and Naïve Bayesian classifier (NB) was the highest scoring traditional method. These are the baseline models compared to the proposed model.
